notes: Identity assessment: supplied text begins with a University of Ghent PDF SOURCE_URL and contains the exact reference title, James R. Schmidt and Derek Besner, University of Waterloo; complete-looking 38-page author manuscript with methods, results, references and figures. It is a primary manuscript of the named work, not an abstract or secondary article. DOI, publication year and final journal pagination are not printed, so those bibliographic details cannot be independently confirmed here. No PDF was supplied. Target unresolved: study_o 2 cannot be reconciled uniquely with the description of a comparison of Stroop effects across mostly congruent and mostly incongruent words. Manuscript p. 8 is theoretical facilitation/interference discussion, not a target results page. Named Experiment 2 (pp. 19–23) instead uses colour-unrelated words, a .50/.25/.17 contingency manipulation and error percentages; its omnibus contingency test is F(2,188) = 12.068, p < .001, partial eta squared .114. Other Experiment 2 candidates: high vs medium errors t(94) = 2.890, p = .005, partial eta squared .082; low vs medium t(94) = 1.929, p = .028 one tailed, partial eta squared .038. These are not a reported comparison of Stroop effect magnitudes. Candidate participant count 95 is recorded only for parent field-scope review, not extracted analytic N. Approximately 20% of trials were excluded for missing the deadline. Reanalysis 1 (p. 10) uses Jacoby et al. Experiment 2a response latencies (16 participants) reorganized by contingency; contingency-by-Stroop interaction F(2,30) = .284, p = .755, partial eta squared .019. Reanalysis 2 (p. 14) uses Jacoby et al. Experiment 2b percentage errors (16 participants); corresponding interaction F(2,30) = .126, p = .882, partial eta squared .004. Neither rearranged contingency interaction is automatically the original proportion-congruency-by-Stroop interaction in the description. Figure 2/3 original-organization plots do not establish a uniquely printed target statistic. No target selected by numbering or numeric agreement. All positive candidate values remain notes only; no N arithmetic or effect conversion performed. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders.
